text.0: I've always been the kind of person who opens a code editor before a presentation. I enjoy building, testing, failing and starting over.
text.1: Over time I realized that a great product isn't just about writing good code. It's about understanding why it exists, who it's for and how to create something people genuinely enjoy using. That's why I expanded into design and marketing.
text.2: What truly motivates me is creating something from scratch. That moment when nothing is decided yet and everything is still possible. That's where I feel I can contribute the most.

hero.statementAccent: Your city is full of art.
hero.statementBody: An app that brings every museum together: plan visits, discover exhibitions, and buy tickets in one place.

problem.title: The problem
problem.lede: Museum information lives scattered across different websites, physical box offices, and social media. Visitors want to plan ahead, but the ecosystem doesn't make it easy. Four data points frame the problem.

referents.title: The hall of references
referents.eyebrow: COMPETITIVE ANALYSIS — EACH ONE EXHIBITS ONE PIECE. NONE SHOWS THE FULL COLLECTION.

architecture.title: The architecture
architecture.eyebrow: INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE · SITE MAP · USER FLOW
architecture.lede: Six spaces organize the app — like the wings of a museum. Each with a clear function, all connected by the same flow: discover, decide, book.

brand.title: The identity
brand.lede: The name joins two worlds: art, organic and expressive, and mus, structured and functional. Art and museum. Emotion and system. The logo tells it in two weights.

stats.phrase: Use mobile to search for museums

items.name: Clara Fernández
items.subtitle: The cultural explorer
items.wants: Discover new exhibitions without tracking ten different websites.
items.frustration: Incomplete information: outdated hours, tickets sold out on arrival.
items.needs: One place to see, decide, and book on the spot.
items.quote: I find out about exhibitions on Instagram... when they're almost over.

items.name: Javier Morales
items.subtitle: The planning student
items.wants: Take advantage of discounts and plan visits that fit his schedule.
items.frustration: Box office queues and not knowing what's worth seeing beforehand.
items.needs: Plan the visit in advance: what to see, when, and at what price.
items.quote: If I could buy the ticket from the couch, I'd visit twice as many museums.

items.name: Museo del Prado
items.label: EXHIBITS
items.domina: Deep curatorial content and a reference-grade digitized collection.
items.falta: Only its own museum. Limited booking and planning.

items.name: Reina Sofía
items.label: EXHIBITS
items.domina: Its own activity calendar and good room information.
items.falta: No cross-discovery or comparison between venues.

items.name: Louvre
items.label: EXHIBITS
items.domina: Highly polished audio guide and indoor maps.
items.falta: Built for the during, not for discovering or planning the before.

items.name: QuickMuseum
items.label: EXHIBITS
items.domina: Quick audio guides for multiple museums in one app.
items.falta: No ticket purchase or planning. Content only.

items.name: CloudGuide
items.label: EXHIBITS
items.domina: Wide catalog of affiliated cultural institutions.
items.falta: Uneven coverage and inconsistent booking experience.

items.name: artmus
items.label: EXHIBITS EVERYTHING
items.domina: Discover + plan + book + buy, for every museum in your city.
items.cartelaTitle: THE PIECE NO ONE WAS EXHIBITING
items.cartelaSubtitle: The full collection, in your pocket.

architecture.title: Book a visit

architecture.title: Events

architecture.title: Profile

brandSection.quoteAccent: Your city is full of art.
brandSection.quoteRest: It just needed a way in.

voices.label: EXPRESSIVE VOICE — SERIF
voices.body: For headlines, the word «art», and moments of emotion. Italics with character.

voices.label: FUNCTIONAL VOICE — SANS
voices.detail: The museum is used in sans
voices.body: For interface, data, and navigation. Clear, geometric, frictionless.

work.label: FROM SKETCH TO CANVAS
work.text1: 26 wireframe screens validated against the user flow before touching color. The component system translates the identity into interface: navy for structure, chartreuse only for action.
work.text2: The exhibition detail screen concentrates 70% of the detected friction — all the information on a single screen, with booking one tap away.

ending.nextDescription: An app that turns any goal into a visible daily action.

hero.headline: Any goal becomes
hero.bodyLine1: A productivity app that makes real progress visible.
hero.bodyLine2: No empty streaks, no endless lists.
hero.bodyLine3: Evidence that the effort is working.

meta.title: THE GOAL
meta.description: Design a productivity app that helps people turn big, abstract goals into concrete daily actions, with visible, tangible progress at every step.

deliverables.label: DELIVERABLES
deliverables.value: IA, wireframes, design system, final UI

caida.title: THE DROP-OFF
caida.lede: Before designing anything, we needed to understand why people abandon their goals. A survey of 120 people revealed four data points that explain it.

cards.title: BLOCKED
cards.phrase: Doesn't know where to start when the goal feels big.

cards.title: COGNITIVE CAUSE
cards.phrase: Choice overload paralyzes the first action.

cards.title: ACTUAL TOOL USED
cards.phrase: Uses a productivity app on a regular basis.

cards.title: WHAT WOULD HELP MOST
cards.phrase: Seeing progress in a visible, tangible way.

caida.quoteText: I know what I have to do, but I don't know if I'm doing it right.

cards.title: Duolingo
cards.subtitle: Gamification
cards.phrase: Turns habit into a game with streaks and levels.

cards.title: Habitica
cards.subtitle: Habit RPG
cards.phrase: Your tasks are quests in a role-playing game.
cards.detail: Community and narrative, little focus on real goals.

cards.title: Streaks
cards.subtitle: Minimalism
cards.phrase: Just streaks. Simple, direct, no distraction.
cards.detail: Visual clarity, but no context or real progress.

cards.title: NEXT
cards.subtitle: Tangible progress
cards.phrase: Every goal becomes a visible daily action.
cards.detail: Real evidence of progress, not just empty streaks.

cards.title: PROGRESS
cards.detail: Visualize real progress, not just checking off tasks.

cards.title: EVIDENCE
cards.detail: Show tangible proof that the effort is working.

cards.title: MOMENTUM
cards.detail: Turn small daily actions into accumulated momentum.

cards.title: COMMUNITY
cards.detail: Share progress with others to sustain commitment.

identidad.title: THE IDENTITY
identidad.lede: The insight became a brand first. NEXT is an arrow: the constant direction toward the next step. An identity system built from the logic of progress, not decoration.

logo.title: One arrow, one grid
logo.text: The symbol is built on a strict grid: every angle, every proportion, follows a mathematical rule. Nothing is arbitrary.

gridColumns.title: TYPEFACE
gridColumns.detail: Geometric sans, clean strokes, no serifs.

gridColumns.title: CHEVRON STROKE
gridColumns.detail: The symbol's angle measures 60°, constant across the brand.

gridColumns.title: SAFE AREA
gridColumns.detail: Clear space equal to the height of the 'N'.

color.title: The rule 70 · 25 · 5.
color.text: The palette works as a hierarchical system: slate and paper dominate, neutrals balance, and color only appears to signal action or alert.
color.contrastAfter: Both meet the minimum contrast across every use.

tone.title: A friend who believes in you. Never a drill sergeant.
tone.text: The research was clear: guilt makes people quit (“when it makes me anxious, I quit”). The tone celebrates real progress and never punishes a relapse.
doPhrases: Today's next step: 20 min of reading.
You're on a 6-day streak. You're doing better than you think.
You couldn't yesterday. Today's a good day to come back.
dontPhrases: You broke your streak. Start from zero.
If you fail, it's because you're not trying hard enough.
